holidays.name: National Candy Corn Day
holidays.description: A day devoted to the polarizing tri-colored candy that people either adore or flatly refuse to eat. Fans celebrate by munching on the waxy, honey-flavored kernels, while skeptics debate whether it counts as candy at all.
holidays.origin: Candy corn was invented in the 1880s by George Renninger of the Wunderle Candy Company in Philadelphia. It was later mass-produced by the Goelitz Candy Company (now Jelly Belly) around 1900, and the day was embraced by candy lovers as an unofficial pre-Halloween tribute.
holidays.funFact: Candy corn was originally marketed to farmers as 'Chicken Feed,' and the boxes carried the slogan 'Something worth crowing for.'

holidays.name: Mischief Night
holidays.description: The night before Halloween eve in parts of the US, Canada, and the UK, when kids and teens traditionally get up to harmless pranks like toilet-papering trees, soaping windows, and ringing doorbells and running away.
holidays.origin: Mischief Night traces back to old British traditions of pranks on the eve of May Day and later Guy Fawkes Night. In North America it settled on October 30 as a prelude to Halloween. In Detroit it became known as 'Devil's Night' and in some regions 'Gate Night' or 'Cabbage Night.'
holidays.funFact: In some parts of northern England, it is called 'Mischief Night' on November 4, the night before Guy Fawkes Day, showing how the tradition shifted across calendars.

holidays.name: Checklists Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the humble checklist, the tool that keeps pilots, surgeons, and grocery shoppers from forgetting things. People are encouraged to make a list, then enjoy the deep satisfaction of ticking off boxes.
holidays.origin: This unofficial observance gained traction among productivity enthusiasts and was inspired by the growing appreciation of checklists in aviation and medicine, popularized by writings such as Atul Gawande's 'The Checklist Manifesto.'
holidays.funFact: The modern pilot checklist originated after the 1935 crash of the Boeing Model 299 prototype, which was deemed 'too much airplane for one man to fly' until pilots created a simple checklist.

holidays.name: Haunted Refrigerator Night
holidays.description: A playful food-and-fright observance where people dig through the back of the fridge to confront the spooky science experiments lurking there. Participants clean out old leftovers and mystery containers just in time for Halloween.
holidays.origin: This tongue-in-cheek unofficial holiday emerged from internet and social media humor, tying the universal fear of forgotten leftovers to the spooky season.
holidays.funFact: Studies on food waste show the average household throws away roughly a third of the food it buys, so many fridges really do hide a few horrors.

holidays.name: Orson Welles 'War of the Worlds' Broadcast Anniversary
holidays.description: Sci-fi and radio fans mark the anniversary of the famous 1938 radio drama that made some listeners believe Martians were invading New Jersey. It's celebrated with listening parties and alien-themed fun.
holidays.origin: On October 30, 1938, Orson Welles and the Mercury Theatre on the Air broadcast an adaptation of H.G. Wells's 'The War of the Worlds' as a Halloween-eve special, presented in the style of breaking news bulletins.
holidays.funFact: Later research suggests the panic was greatly exaggerated by newspapers, which were eager to discredit radio as a rival for advertising money.
